preamble: Lenition of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the palatal approximant [j] removes the oral closure while keeping the palatal place. The Proto-Slavic reflex of *dj, written *ď and usually reconstructed as a palatal stop [ɟ(ː)], became j in Slovene (méja 'border'), against Shtokavian đ (međa), Polish and Slovak dz and East Slavic ž. The phonetic value of *ď is debated (palatal stop or palatalized dental), and the change is confined to the western South Slavic area, so it is rare.

examples.note: Compare Serbo-Croatian mèđa, Russian межа́, Polish miedza.
Compare Bulgarian пре́жда, Russian пря́жа, Polish przędza.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Oti-Volta to Core Eastern Oti-Volta (Nateni, Mbelime, Ditammari, Byali)

examples.to: Nateni yóódī, Mbelime yóódè, Ditammari kūyōó
examples.note: Forms in Eddyshaw's transcription: j = [ɟ], y = [j], ɩ ʋ = [ɪ ʊ], a tilde below a vowel marks nasalization, ' marks a glottalized vowel; POV = Proto-Oti-Volta; the final syllable of nouns is a noun-class suffix. Gurma keeps the stop (Moba jóól̀).
Eddyshaw: in Core Eastern Oti-Volta *j becomes y; Waama instead has c, and Western Oti-Volta z.
